d: Nonproliferative, hormone-driven change of premenopausal breasts made of cysts, stromal fibrosis and apocrine metaplasia; bilateral, lumpy and tender before menses, with no added cancer risk.
A monotonous, clonal proliferation partly filling ducts that shares some features of low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ; it raises the risk of invasive cancer about four to five times.
A biphasic tumor of intralobular stroma with stromal overgrowth forming leaf-like fronds; it occurs around age 50, grows fast, recurs if incompletely excised and can be malignant.
A benign papillary tumor in a large subareolar lactiferous duct, with fibrovascular cores covered by luminal and myoepithelial cells; the classic cause of bloody discharge from one duct.
Necrosis of breast fat after trauma or surgery; released fatty acids bind calcium (saponification), and foamy macrophages and fibrosis form a firm, calcified mass that mimics cancer.

A CD30-positive, ALK-negative T-cell lymphoma arising in the fluid or capsule around textured implants, usually presenting years after placement as a late fluid collection; treated by removing implant and capsule.
Supernumerary nipples along the embryonic milk line from axilla to groin, the most common congenital breast anomaly; they are often mistaken for moles.
